dialog.body: Public Works storm line, this is Lorraine. How can I help you?
Good morning. Kindly forgive me for calling on a Saturday. I understand City Hall is closed today, but I was told this number is answered during storms. Is that correct?
That's right, this line's open for storm calls even when the offices are closed. What's going on?
The water is standing in the street in front of my house again. It is the storm drain, I believe. The street flooded last month as well, and nothing whatsoever was done about it.
Okay. I'm sorry, that's aggravating. Let me get the address. Where are you?
444 Ayrault Street, on the Hill. It is near the corner, not far from the church.
444 Ayrault Street. And is the water getting into the house, or is it out in the road?

Thank goodness, the house itself has stayed dry. It is the street, and it comes up over the curb on our side. But I should not have to stand at the window watching it, every time we have a heavy rain.
No, understood. So the street is flooded, the house is dry, and this also happened last month. Have I got that right?
You have it exactly right. Kindly note that it is the same drain both times.
I'll note it's the same drain. Is the grate covered with anything, leaves, debris?

It was covered with leaves, yes. This morning I went out with my rake, and then, I confess, with my hands, and I cleared the grate myself. The water went down nicely. But only for about ten minutes, and then it came back up again.
So you cleared it by hand and it drained for a little bit, then backed up again.
Yes. Which tells me the trouble is not only the leaves. Something is blocked below, in the pipe. I am no engineer, but that is what it looks like to me.

That could well be it. Leaves wash right back in during a storm like this one, but if it backs up after you've cleared it, the line underneath may be slow or plugged. A crew would have to look at that.
That is precisely what I wish to ask you. Will a work order be opened for this? And kindly tell me, for what date?

I'm opening one right now, so yes, it will be on the books today. As for the date, I'll tell you how it works. The crews are working the worst flooding first, so with the storm only wrapping up today, I'd say look for somebody early next week. I'd rather give you a window than a promise on a specific day.
Early next week. Very well. I would like that written down, if you would be so kind.
It's written down. Work order for the storm drain at 444 Ayrault Street, recurring flooding, same drain as last month, grate cleared by resident but backing up again. Did I miss anything?

No, that is complete. I do wish to say, I am a little tired of this. I lost a good part of my morning to it. I was looking for a file, with the papers from last month, when I first reported this, and I spent an entire hour searching and could not find it.
Oh, that's frustrating. Do you remember who you spoke to last month, or about when?
I cannot say with certainty. That is the whole difficulty. I believe it was in the middle of the month, but I have no name and no number to give you.
That's okay. You don't need the old paperwork for this. I've got your address and the description, and I'll put in the notes that it's a repeat so whoever picks it up knows it's not the first time.
Thank you. That is a comfort, though a small one. It has been a long while that this street has flooded.
I hear you. Now, can I get a number in case the crew needs to reach you about it?
Certainly. It is 401-555-0195.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, zero-one-nine-five. Is that a cell?
Yes, it is my cell telephone. I will keep it with me.
Good. One more thing, while that water's up, please stay out of it if you can. Storm drain water can have all kinds of things in it, and you can't see what's under it.
I understand. I will keep my shoes dry from now on. But I could not bear to watch the leaves sit there.
Fair enough. And if the water ever does start coming toward the house, call this line right back, and I'll make sure that gets flagged as urgent.
I will do so. Kindly tell me, will anyone call me before they come?
Possibly, it depends on the crew. They usually just show up and work on the drain, since it's in the street. If they need to get hold of you, they'll use that number.
Very well. Then I shall wait to see them early next week, and if they do not come, I shall call again.
That's fair, and if you do, mention it's the Ayrault Street drain and that a work order went in on Saturday. That'll help them find it fast.
Saturday, the Ayrault Street drain. I have written it on the pad by the telephone, so I will not lose it this time.
Good plan. Anything else I can do for you this morning?
No, that is all. Thank you for answering on a Saturday. Kindly have a good day.
You too, Ms. Semedo. Take care, and stay dry.
